headline: Britain launches a massive £150bn electricity grid overhaul
standfirst: The country is building thousands of miles of new power lines to secure energy and hit

steps.label: What happened
steps.text: Britain is beginning a massive upgrade to its electricity grid to build vital new power lines.

steps.label: How we got here
steps.text: The country needs five times more infrastructure to meet climate targets and energy security needs.

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.text: The project aims to stop future energy shocks, but it will cause household bills to rise.

steps.label: What to watch
steps.text: Construction is moving forward, but local opposition to the new infrastructure is growing.

caption:
Britain is planning a massive overhaul of its electricity grid to improve energy security.

The £150 billion megaproject involves installing thousands of miles of new power lines across the country. While it is designed to help hit climate targets, the short-term cost means energy bills will likely increase for many households. Opponents are already mobilizing against the scale of the construction.

Do you think the long-term energy security is worth the short-term increase in your bills?
